modelResponse.episodeSummary: A 61-year-old male with ischemic cardiomyopathy and LVEF 25% experienced an 8-second episode of monomorphic ventricular tachycardia at a rate of 182 bpm. The patient presented with progressive dyspnea and volume overload but no acute chest pain. Hemodynamics were borderline with a systolic blood pressure of 88 mmHg. ECG showed wide monomorphic QRS, AV dissociation, and occasional capture/fusion beats.
modelResponse.mostLikelyEtiologyAndClinicalContext: The most likely etiology is re-entrant ventricular tachycardia related to structural heart disease. This is supported by the patient's history of ischemic cardiomyopathy with severely reduced LVEF (25%), prior inferior MI, and the ECG findings of monomorphic VT with AV dissociation and fusion beats, consistent with a re-entrant circuit within scarred myocardium.
contributingFactors: Severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (25%)
